sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:3340
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 934 of 2004

Revisionist :- Jugun Prasad
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Revisionist :- Satyendra Narayan Singh,R.P. Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.

1. Heard Sri Pramod Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the revisionist and Sri R.K. Gupta,
learned AGA for the State.

2. This criminal revision by convict Jugun Prasad has been filed challenging the order dated 10.04.2001 passed by the trial court in Criminal case no. 1027 of 1994 (State vs. Jugun Prasad) by which he was convicted for offence under sections 7(1)/16(1)(A)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was sentenced to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment and Rs. 1,000/-
as fine and further the order dated 23.02.2004 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 23 of 2001,
confirming the order of the trial court and dismissing the appeal.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant facts are as below:-
The food inspector found the accused selling 'ice candies'.

He introduced himself and took sample of 18 pieces of ice candy, after paying the cost and handed over the notice (form no. 6) to the seller; the sample was kept in three separate bottles with Jugun Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133442931/
1 the preservatives added to it; the samples were wrapped and sealed as per the rules and sent for chemical examination; the State Forensic Laboratory chemically examined the same and found the samples to be adulterated article of food; after obtaining sanction from the C.M.O., a complaint was filed against the seller-Jugun Prasad; The matter proceeded on the basis of the above complaint before the court of Magistrate; the statement under sections 244 and 246 Cr.P.C. were recorded; the food inspector and one more were examined by the prosecution; certain documentary evidence was produced; after completion of evidence, the statement under section 313 Cr.P.C. were recorded and after hearing both the sides, the learned trial court pronounced the judgment and order convicting the accused and sentencing him with imprisonment of six months and fine of Rs. 1,000/-; the accused preferred an appeal before the superior court but his appeal too was dismissed and the order of the trial court was confirmed.

sentences.text:
4. The main contentions of the revisionist are that the mandatory provisions of section 10(7) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act were not duly complied and no independent witness was procured at the time of sampling; the provisions of section 13(7) of the Act and connected Rules 17 and 18 of the Act were not complied with; the procedure adopted was vitiated; it is further contended that the food analyst did not mention that how low the percentage of sugar was found in the ice candy; whether this deficiency was injurious for health of an individual or not; the provisions of section 21(i) of the Act were also ignored and that the order was passed in a mechanical manner,
ignoring the provisions of law including the provisions of section 11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Rules 7 and 10 of the Act; the prosecution could not procure any witness except food analyst who was not an independent witness, hence the order be allowed to be set aside.
5. From perusal of the records as well as the judgment, it is clear that the prosecution case is that the sample of the ice candy was sent to the food analyst through parcel but the prosecution failed to produce the receipt to prima facie establish that in fact the samples were sent to food analyst,
without any delay.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Rules 7 and 10
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. There is another forceful contention that provisions of section 13 of the Act were not duly complied with by the prosecution.
7. I went through the provisions of section 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

This section provides that the public analyst shall deliver a report to the local health authority of the result of the analysis of article of the food and that on receipt of the report of the result of the analysis to the effect that the article of food was found adulterated, the local health authority shall,
after institution of the prosecution against the persons from whom the sample was taken, forward a copy of the food analysis report informing that he has right to apply to the court concerned to get the sample re-analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory.
8.
I went through whole of the judgment passed by the trial court.

The trial court has nowhere referred to those provisions of law and has not given any finding whether the mandatory provisions of section 13 of the Act were complied with by the public analyst or the local health authority.

From Jugun Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133442931/
2 the relevant portion of the judgment passed by the appellate court, it appears that the appellate courts on the basis of a postal receipt presumed that copy of the report of food analyst was sent to the accused by the local health authority.

sentences.text: In my opinion, the court ought to have asked for a copy of the letter, by which the accused was clearly informed of his right to apply to the Central Food Laboratory for re-examination of the sample.
In absence of those papers, it cannot be presumed that the accused was duly informed of his right to apply for re-analysis of sample within the period of 10 days from the date of the receipt.
The learned trial court as well as the appellate court has failed to mention the date of the receipt of copy of the test report.

In my opinion the statutory rights given to the accused assume more importance in the background of the fact that in this case, the ice candy was put into category of adulterated food just because it did not contain the minimum 10% of the sugar, as is prescribed by the Rules.
Analyst report simply says that sugar was below 10%, which is minimum.
It does not say what was exactly the percentage of sugar in the ice candy.

In view of the above report of the public analyst, the revisionist has argued that the ice candy was prepared by intervention of human agency and that whole of the process is not so technically sound and mechanized that it can exclude any variations in the percentage.
If the percentage is very low, the intent can be attached to an offender.
However, when the percentage is marginally at variance with the prescribed limit or is negligibly different the accused should have been granted benefit of doubt.
I went through the papers on record.
The public analyst has said that sugar content was less than 10% of the minimum prescribed limit but it does not give any description as to what was actually the percentage of the sugar in ice candy.
9. In view of the above, I find substance in the arguments.

The learned trial court as well as the learned appellate court failed to see that public analyst has not described the actual percentage of sugar content in the ice candy and has simply said that it was below 10%.
In my view, the chemical analyst cannot act as a layman and he has to describe the actual percentage to lend credibility to his chemical report.
He has not described the chemical process by which this percentage was determined.
The report of the food analyst which is actually most important documentary evidence in cases of food adulteration should contain all relevant facts.
More often then not the food analyst's report is a piece of evidence which forms the basis of prosecution under the Act, hence its significance cannot be undermined.
The report must mention all essential scientific fact to maintain its credibility.

In my view, the order of the trial court as well as the appellate court are liable to be set-aside and the revision is therefore allowed.
10. The sureties, if any, are hereby discharged from their liabilities and the accused is acquitted of the charges under sections 7(1)/16(1)(A)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
11.
Let a copy of order be sent to the court concerned.
